results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices 20% as supply tightens | Five Nines
highlights:
By September 16, 2026, the AI neocloud expansion had reached a pricing inflection. BigGo Finance reported that Nebius said it will raise GPU cloud prices by an average of 20 percent from October 1, covering H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips, with B300 rising from $7.85 to $9.50 per GPU-hour. The announcement pushed Nebius shares up nearly 7 percent in after-hours trading.

That increase followed a financing and siting rush that enterprises watched closely. On August 4, 2026, Sharon AI signed a five-year, $373 million contract with a global AI platform customer for AI cloud services, according to tech-insider.org. The first deployment uses 2,048 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs hosted in NEXTDC data centres in Melbourne and Sydney.

...

The latest price signal matters for enterprises purchasing AI compute. Nebius's increase is its second since May, and it follows auction tests where customers paid 15 to 20 percent above the previous maximum listed price for scarce Blackwell capacity. Nebius also said demand visibility now extends beyond 24 months. tech-insider.org reported that committed-contract discounts can reach 60 percent off list price but require multi-year commitments, and recommended hybrid architectures that keep general workloads on hyperscalers while routing GPU-intensive jobs to neoclouds.

highlights:
# Nebius: the cost of a reported price reset.

A customer-reported October 1 increase puts GPU budgets under review. The next question is whether the new rates apply—and what useful work costs after the change.

## The research call

Budget for the possibility; verify the applicable quote. The preserved public capture still shows the existing rates. The higher figures below come from a customer repost of a purported email. They remain unverified, and they are not inserted into observed price history. A list-price move alone cannot establish realized pricing, utilization or provider margins.

All bars start at $0 and use the same $10 scale. Public capture: Sep. 17, 00:32 UTC (Sep. 16 Pacific).

Solid blue: dated public observation. Outlined: customer-reported future rate, not authenticated. These are paired price levels, not a measured time series. Download chart PNG ↓ · Data CSV ↓

## A report, with a meaningful budget impact.

The repost describes increases of 16.9%–21.0% across four NVIDIA GPU types, reportedly effective October 1, 2026. The original customer email has not been authenticated.

For B200, the reported move from $7.15 to $8.50 adds $1.35 per GPU-hour. At 1,000 GPU-hours that is $1,350, before other charges and discounts. The size of the budget sensitivity justifies a contract check; it does not verify the notice.

## Separate posted prices from pricing power.

A higher on-demand rate may matter to marginal buyers while reserved contracts and negotiated discounts behave differently. To evaluate pricing power, follow comparable offers, available capacity and realized contract economics together.

A provider-specific reset is also different from a market-wide move. No matched cross-provider panel or customer-billing evidence is established by this notice. This edition makes no revenue, earnings or margin forecast.

...

The public landing-page quotes do not attach a region to each row. These are the regions named in the customer report; confirm the provider documentation and your actual contract.

results.title: GPU Cloud Services Surge in Price: Nebius Raises Prices Again by 20%, Computing Power Supply Side Gains Bargaining Power | Bitget News
highlights:
From October 1st, Nebius will raise prices for its entire GPU cloud service line by approximately 20%, with multiple chips from H100 to B300 seeing increases. This marks the second round of price hikes in recent months, and the cumulative increase for B300 has reached 56%. Demand visibility extends beyond 24 months, with customers eager to purchase Blackwell computing power, even willing to pay a premium in auctions. The supply-demand imbalance for AI computing power is reshaping the entire industry’s negotiation landscape, as bargaining power is quietly shifting to the supply side.

Nebius has announced a comprehensive price increase for its GPU cloud services effective October 1, with an average uptick of about 20%. Coupled with NVIDIA’s strong quarterly earnings, this drove Nebius stock nearly 7% higher in after-hours trading, further confirming market sentiment that AI computing power supply remains tight relative to demand.

This round of price adjustments covers multiple chip models including H100, H200, B200, and B300, and marks Nebius' second price hike since May this year. The market interprets this as a strong signal that AI computing power demand remains overheated while supply stays tight. As a result, Coreweave shares rose nearly 4% after hours, the optical communication sector generally strengthened, with AAOI and Credo Technology each up nearly 3%, Marvell Technology and Astera Labs up more than 2%, and Coherent up nearly 2%.

...

## Price Increase Details: Substantial Hikes for Multiple GPU Models

According to pricing screenshots circulating on X, this round of price hikes is significant. The H100 now costs $4.50 per GPU hour, up from $3.85—a gain of about 16.9%; H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase); B200 increases from $7.15 to $8.50 (approximately 18.9%); and B300 jumps from $7.85 to $9.50 (about 21% increase).

This marks Nebius's second price hike within a few months. In May of this year, the company announced an average 29% increase in on-demand capacity prices and a 51% increase in preemptible capacity. For instance, B300’s hourly price has now climbed about 56% from the pre-May level of approximately $6.10.

In a May email to customers, Nebius stated that the adjustment "reflects the sustained, strong demand for high-end GPU computing power. Even after the updated pricing, Nebius remains one of the most competitively priced GPU infrastructure providers on the market." According to Stocktwits, as of press time, Nebius has yet to publicly respond to the latest price hike rumors.

...

Market analysts point out that this price hike reflects deeper supply and demand dynamics. According to X user @MelvinInvests, Nebius previously attempted manual price adjustments, but management indicated that strong demand still made the adjustments insufficient to balance supply and demand. Subsequently, the company conducted auction trials for scarce Blackwell computing power, with customers paying 15%–20% above the prior highest prices to secure access.

results.title: GPU price increase in 2026: why AWS costs keep rising | AI Compute Marketplace | Compare GPU Cloud & Data Centers | ComputeStacker Insights
highlights:
## Key takeaways

- GPU prices are increasing across the industry in 2026 as AI demand outpaces chip supply.
- AWS has increased EC2 Capacity Block GPU pricing twice in 2026: once in January by around 15% and again in July by around 20%.
- According to AWS’s own pricing page, there is another price hike due in October 2026.
- The price hikes only apply to reserved Capacity Block pricing, not on-demand or Savings Plans.
- There are legitimate alternatives to AWS reserved capacity for buyers to consider.

...

First, AWS increased EC2 Capacity Block prices by roughly 15% on January 4, 2026. According to DataCenterDynamics, this was the first price increase for this product ever.

The p5e.48xlarge GPU instance has increased its hourly price in almost all regions from $34.61 to $39.80. With p5en.48xlarge, the price jumped from $36.18 to $41.61. Even US West got a rise from $43.26 to $49.75.

The second price increase occurred on July 1. They estimated the increase to be around 20% and applied it to the newest generations of the company’s products, not just to the existing H100-based fleet.

Here is how AWS’s own live pricing page shows prices today for its GPU instance families:

| Instance type | Chip | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | Blackwell Ultra | $14.04/accelerator-hr |
| P6-B200 | Blackwell | $12.355/accelerator-hr |
| P5en | H200 | $6.865/hr (US) |
| P5e | H200 | $5.97/hr |
| P5 | H100 | $5.191/hr (US) |
| P4de | A100 | $2.214/hr (US) |

There is even more. As AWS states on its pricing page, the next price change will happen in October 2026. Articles covering the two price increases of 2026 never mention this aspect.

AWS has said not much about the reasons behind price changes. They were just attributed to “periodic pricing updates tied to supply and demand”.

...

Not all AWS GPU users bore these price increases equally. The price increase was applicable only to the Capacity Block category, which is a reservation product of AWS offering guaranteed GPU capacity within a certain period.

Pricing models like the price increase have not affected on-demand and Savings Plans, and knowing that will help you decide which pricing model you should choose yourself.

The reason behind the existence of Capacity Block is that there is some extra value in the guaranteed access to scarce GPU capacity. You pay not only for the compute but for the guaranteed access to it as well, which is why AWS can raise the prices in this category.

...

Does the AWS price increase affect on-demand instances too?

No, AWS restricted both 2026 increases to Capacity Blocks, the reservation offering of AWS. The changes did not affect on-demand prices and savings, although this might change with the upcoming October announcement.

results.title: The same GPU, at very different prices · infratoapp
highlights:
30 GPU models are rented on-demand by 3 or more of the providers listed here. On every one of them, the providers disagree about the price — and on most, they disagree by more than a rounding error.

The median gap between the cheapest and dearest seller of an identical card is 3.8×. The widest is the V100-16GB: $0.24 per GPU-hour at Verda (DataCrunch) against $2.85 at Runcrate, a gap of 11.8×. An H100 SXM 80GB — the card most of this market is actually built on — runs from $2.16 to $6.16 across 13 sellers, a gap of 2.8×.

These are headline on-demand rates, before any commitment discount, for the same part. Not a similar part, not a different memory configuration, and not one region against another.

...

The newest parts — B200, B300 and H200 — vary by an average of 2.8× across their sellers. Everything older varies by 4.7×.

results.title: The same H100 rents for $1.79 an hour from one provider and $10.00 from another. | Mercatus AI | The Open Intelligence Exchange
highlights:
The same H100 rents for $1.79 an hour from one provider and $10.00 from another.

Not a different GPU. Not a different region. Same 80GB SXM5 card, on-demand, this week.

We track 27 providers on the Mercatus GPU Index. Here is where the market sits as of September 13:

H100: $3.84/hr average, range $1.79 to $12.52
H200: $4.43/hr average, range $2.25 to $11.71
B200: $6.39/hr average, range $3.74 to $16.14

On an 8-GPU H100 node running around the clock, that spread is $11,400 a month at the cheapest provider and $58,400 at the most expensive. A $47,000 gap on identical hardware.

The gap between an average H100 node and an average B200 node is $15,000.

A posted rate card tells you what one seller wants, not what the market price is. Same lesson as tokens.

The current spot leasing price for NVIDIA B200 GPUs is approximately $5.72 per hour, having risen continuously over the past two months and is only about 10% lower than the peak of $6.10 in March.
